(Search snippet content)

Sir Keir Starmer delivered his final Prime Minister's Questions on Wednesday (15 July 2026), receiving a rare standing ovation from Parliament.

The Hillsborough Law passed the House of Commons in one of Starmer's final acts as Prime Minister, after ministers agreed its duty of candour would apply to the intelligence services.

DIRECT QUOTE — Sir Keir Starmer: said he was "proud" to bring back the legislation.

- The law imposes a duty on public authorities and officials to act with candour, transparency and frankness, to prevent institutional cover-ups.
- It fulfils a Labour manifesto pledge from 2024 and is legislation Starmer championed since his time as Director of Public Prosecutions.
- Burnham's transition team has begun Civil Service access talks authorised by Starmer, despite reports of a "frosty" initial meeting between the two men over defence investment plans.
- Burnham won the Makerfield by-election on 18 June 2026 to return to Westminster; was declared Labour leader on Friday 17 July; formally accepts the King's invitation to form a government on Monday 20 July.
